issues.location: first gloss in the cardinal-infinity characterization theorem
issues.finding: The formula states that the cardinal of A is not in omega, but the following gloss says A is not a natural number. A can be a non-ordinal finite set, so the gloss is false and does not express the stated infinitude criterion.
issues.proposed_resolution: Gloss the formula as A not being a finite set, retaining the formula and the three-way equivalence.

issues.location: proof that every infinite cardinal is a limit ordinal
issues.finding: The source cites the finite-cardinal equinumerosity proposition as a reason that the predecessor beta of an infinite successor ordinal is infinite. That proposition does not establish this inference; the needed fact is that the successor of a finite ordinal is finite.
issues.proposed_resolution: Replace that citation with the finite-successor argument and state that the cardinal of the predecessor does not exceed it before concluding the successor is not a cardinal.

translation_treatment: The target corrects the gloss of cardinal infinitude and replaces the inapposite predecessor citation with the finite-successor argument, preserving the surrounding formulas and result. Frozen source bytes remain unchanged.
